sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and design note
sections.what: Pulls in the house colours, font and wordmark, and the type describing the slide context. A comment at the top says the cover is a solid black panel with no footer.
sections.why: The comment says photography will come in a later pass, so the plain black panel is deliberate for now.

sections.name: TitleSlide
sections.title: Cover panel with title and date
sections.what: Draws the black cover with the wordmark and red underline, the title reading the industry name followed by Capital Projects and Cost and Schedule Overruns, and the month and year beneath it.
sections.why: Names the deck and its subject on the first page.
sections.watch_out: The date is the viewing date, not the date the data was collected.

summary: The cover page of the industry deck: a black panel with the house wordmark, the deck title and the current month and year.
purpose: Introduces the deck with the industry name and a date.
why: The comment says the cover has no footer or source line by design, and the black panel is a placeholder until photography is added.
how: 1. Reads the industry name from the slide context. 2. Makes a date label for the current month and year in English. 3. Draws a black panel with the wordmark and a red underline at the top left. 4. Places the title and date in the centre left.
inputs: The industry name from the slide context, and the computer's current date.
outputs: One cover slide. No data is saved or sent anywhere.
risks: The date is the day the page is viewed, not when the data was collected, so the cover changes each month even if nothing else does. The title wording is fixed and assumes every industry is about capital projects with overruns.
debug: If the date looks wrong, check the device clock. If the title reads oddly, check the industry name passed in from the slide context.
